pr.title: Stabilize `min_exhaustive_patterns`
pr.author: Nadrieril

processing.reason: PR 122792 (`Stabilize min_exhaustive_patterns`) does not contain a source-grounded lifetime/CFG miscompilation to reproduce. The only SimplifyCfg-related changes are updated expected-output files `tests/mir-opt/building/match/never_patterns.opt{1,2,3}.SimplifyCfg-initial.after.mir`; no SimplifyCfg implementation was changed. The old and new dumps are semantically equivalent for every well-defined input: `opt1/opt2/opt3` take `&Result<u32, Void>`, whose only inhabited variant is `Ok(u32)`, so the removed/retained `FakeRead(ForMatchedPlace(..))`, unreachable `Err` blocks, and single-case discriminant switches are never executed. The `match_pair.rs` edit only makes the uninhabited by-value variant arm irrefutable during lowering; for valid values it removes an unreachable check, not a live branch. The by-value vs not-by-value (reference/pointer/union) distinction is enforced by compile-time exhaustiveness checking, and a not-by-value case such as `&Result<u32, !>` still requires the extra arm, so no defined runtime input can reach a branch that the PR's lowering would collapse. Distinguishing the incorrect collapse would require an invalid value (e.g. a fabricated `&Void`/reference to an uninhabited variant) that fails Miri or would be arbitrary UB, and manufacturing a source function that routes `Err` to the `Ok` block would not be the actual historical transformation. Therefore no valid original/transformed pair with differing defined observable results can be built and Miri-validated.

analysis.originalLogic: SimplifyCfg runs immediately after match building and removes redundant control flow. Before stabilization, matches on a reference to an empty-containing type kept a discriminant switch and dead arms, e.g. `bb0: { PlaceMention(_1); _2 = discriminant((*_1)); switchInt(move _2) -> [0: bb2, 1: bb3, otherwise: bb1]; }`, with separate `FakeRead(ForMatchedPlace(None), _1); unreachable;` blocks. After stabilization the builder can emit a `falseEdge -> [real: bb4, imaginary: bb1];` in `bb0` and a single-case switch `switchInt(move _2) -> [1: bb3, otherwise: bb2];`, or, when only one path remains, SimplifyCfg drops the switch entirely so `bb0` directly executes `StorageLive(_3); ... return;`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically/incorrectly, a simplification could retain a now-redundant discriminant switch and its unreachable `FakeRead` arm for a match whose empty variants are by-value uninhabited, or could delete a live `falseEdge` target / a reachable return block. The correct simplification preserves the `falseEdge` real/imaginary targets and only collapses the switch when its discriminant set has a single live case; block renumbering and reordering of `falseEdge` relative to `discriminant` are expected outputs of the new lowering, not semantic changes. It must not collapse a live branch for a not-by-value empty type such as `&Result<u32, !>`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR for `match`/never-pattern matches on `&Result<u32, Void>`-style scrutinees, containing `PlaceMention`, `falseEdge`, `FakeRead(ForMatchedPlace(..))`, `discriminant`, and `switchInt`; both by-value and dereferenced empty types; functions `opt1`, `opt2`, `opt3` in `tests/mir-opt/building/match/never_patterns.rs`.
analysis.summary: After min_exhaustive_patterns, match lowering for never patterns over empty-containing types emits simpler CFGs (`falseEdge` and single-case `switchInt`). SimplifyCfg is expected to reduce these to the sole live path, removing dead `FakeRead`/unreachable blocks, while preserving the `falseEdge` imaginary target. This is a stabilization-driven MIR-test update, not a confirmed pass bug fix.
analysis.trigger: Post-lowering MIR of a match on an empty-containing type where the match has a `falseEdge` and/or a `switchInt` with only one live case, plus dead `FakeRead(ForMatchedPlace(..))` blocks.
preconditions: `falseEdge` real and imaginary targets must both be preserved until unwinding/cleanup handling.
A `switchInt` may only be removed when exactly one discriminant path is live.
Do not perform the collapse for empty types that are not matched by value (references/pointers/unions).
SimplifyCfg is a CFG pass: block numbering is not stable and must not be encoded as semantic identity.
pitfalls: The after-pass `.mir` dumps show the discriminant switch moved from `bb0` to `bb1` and the `falseEdge` moved into `bb0`; tests must not rely on block order.
In the fully-collapsed case (`opt2`) all switch and unreachable blocks disappear from the after-pass dump.
`FakeRead(ForMatchedPlace(..))` on an unreachable arm is dead but must not be reordered before the live path.
The imaginary target of `falseEdge` is part of semantics and must not be dropped.
analysis.testStrategy: Use `tests/mir-opt/building/match/never_patterns.opt{1,2,3}.SimplifyCfg-initial.after.mir` full-MIR dumps. Check that `falseEdge -> [real: ..., imaginary: ...]` survives, that the single-case `switchInt(move _2) -> [1: ..., otherwise: ...]` is preserved, and that the fully constant case has a straight-line `return` with no switch. Add a by-value vs `&`/pointer contrast so the collapse is only expected for by-value empty types.
